definitions.gloss: one's place; one's station; one's standing; one's limits
definitions.explanation: One's social position, abilities, or means. Often used in expressions about knowing one's limits or acting within one's means.

examples.japanese: {身|み}の{程|ほど}をわきまえた{行動|こうどう}をするべきだ。
examples.english: You should act in accordance with your station.

examples.japanese: {身|み}の{程|ほど}{知|し}らずにも{社長|しゃちょう}に{意見|いけん}してしまったが、{意外|いがい}にも{受|う}け{入|い}れてもらえた。
examples.english: I had the audacity to offer my opinion to the CEO, but surprisingly it was accepted.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly appears in set expressions. {身|み}の{程|ほど}を{知|し}る (to know one's place) and {身|み}の{程|ほど}{知|し}らず (not knowing one's place) are the most frequent. Can sound harsh or old-fashioned when used to tell someone to stay in their lane.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身|み}の{程|ほど}を{知|し}る (to know one's place)
- {身|み}の{程|ほど}{知|し}らず (not knowing one's place; presumptuous)
- {身|み}の{程|ほど}をわきまえる (to be aware of one's standing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {分際|ぶんざい}: one's status/position — harsher, used to put someone down
- {身分|みぶん}: social standing, status — more neutral, refers to official rank or position
